subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@pulsemed.com>, Kyle Dawson <kyle.d@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, Aug 1, 2026 at 2:05 PM PDT
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Kyle —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything please flag.

Pain points you called out:
- Latency variability and tail latency during peak hours (real-time triage workflows can’t tolerate >250ms P95).
- Concerns about data isolation and keys for PHI/RWD pipelines (must be customer-managed KMS).
- Existing cost unpredictability on public endpoints — need predictable committed cost and capacity.

Goals we heard:
- Dedicated GPU capacity (reserved) with network isolation (VPC + private control plane).
- Predictable throughput for real-time endpoints and room to scale for batch/ingest spikes.
- SLA that covers uptime and latency SLOs for production traffic.

Proposed high-level configuration (we’ll follow with a one-page summary and SOW):
- Baseline: 8 x A100 80GB (dedicated pool) pinned to your account/tenant.
- Autoscale/burst: automatic burst up to 16 GPUs for sustained peak windows with warm pool to avoid cold starts.
- Networking: VPC peering + private control plane; option for on-prem/private deployment if required.
- Security: customer-managed KMS (BYOK), audit logs, SOC 2 artifacts.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime for the Dedicated cluster + support (24/7 P1 escalation).

Next steps / owners:
1) I’ll circulate a short capacity summary + draft SOW (attached) — Ben (today, EOD PT).
2) PulseMed to confirm target production date and expected token/req volumes so we can finalize sizing — Sara/Kyle (ASAP).
3) Internal alignment: Marissa to coordinate pricing/legal.
4) Proposed follow-up: technical kickoff (1 hour) week of Aug 10 to walk infra/rollout/canary plan.

Open questions we still have:
- Do you require data residency restricted to us-east-1?
- Any minimum monthly commit or billing cadence preferences for procurement?

Attachments: pulsemed_dedicated_capacity_summary.pdf, SOW-draft-pulsemed.pdf (first pass)

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@pulsemed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Dawson <kyle.d@pulsemed.com>
Date: Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 9:22 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — this looks great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: yes, must be restricted to us-east-1 for our PHI processing.
- Compliance: we’ll need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a runbook for incident response before production.
- Traffic: expected baseline ~5–8M tokens/day, peak up to ~12M tokens/day during heavy days. Concurrency: typical 60–80 reqs/sec, peaks ~250 reqs/sec.
- Staging: we’d like a staging mirror of the Dedicated environment for end-to-end testing prior to cutover.

Procurement: I’m pulling in our procurement lead (I’ll share contact info) — we’ll need a SOW and an order form. Once we have the SOW and pricing we can route to procurement/IT.

We’re generally comfortable with the proposed config but would like the staging + SOC2 artifacts before signing.

Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of ML Ops | PulseMed
sara@pulsemed.com | +1 (617) 555-0137

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Kyle Dawson <kyle.d@pulsemed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, Aug 3, 2026 at 11:18 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Sara — all clear. Quick updates based on your notes: 

- Residency: we can pin all Dedicated instances to us-east-1 and enforce region-level placement for data and compute.
- Compliance: attaching the SOC 2 summary and our runbook excerpt in the capacity summary PDF. We’ll also include a list of artifacts (logs, config, access controls).
- Staging: we’ll provision a staging mirror with identical config (smaller commit, e.g., 2x A100) to validate rollouts and run your test suite prior to production.
- Sizing / burst: Given your peak numbers, baseline 8x A100 with autoscale to 16 should cover steady-state + peaks with headroom. We’ll also enable prefix/KV caching for repeat traffic to reduce cost and improve tail latency.
- SLA: Standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% with 24/7 P1 support and an SLO for P95 latency targets; we’ll include a latency-based runbook for mitigation (auto-fallback to a compatible hosted variant during partial outages).

Pricing (ballpark for planning):
- Dedicated baseline (8 x A100 80GB reserved): $45,000/month commit.
- Autoscale bursts billed on usage above the commit (we’ll model expected token volumes in the final quote).
- Staging mirror (2 x A100): one-time setup + $6,000/month.

What I’m attaching: pulsemed_dedicated_capacity_summary.pdf (configuration, security, SLA, network diagram), SOW-draft-pulsemed.pdf (first pass).

Next steps:
- Review SOW + pricing with procurement and share any redlines (Sara).
- I’ll loop Legal and Solutions with Marissa for final pricing/legal review.
- Technical kickoff: propose Tue Aug 11 at 10am ET — does that work?

Ben
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: pulsemed_dedicated_capacity_summary.pdf, SOW-draft-pulsemed.pdf

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Aug 3, 2026 at 2:46 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Ben — thanks for the summary. A couple internal notes: 

- Pricing looks directionally reasonable; I’ll run margin and reference comps. Legal will want to review the SOW redlines specific to KMS/BYOK and data residency (I’ll set up a 30-min sync with Legal & Security).
- Ops: we should prepare a canary rollout plan for the Dedicated cutover (traffic-shift steps, rollback triggers, telemetry). I can draft the canary playbook with Solutions Eng.
- Sales ops: get me the expected contract length (12 vs 24 months) and any requested billing cadence so I can create the ARR/commit model.

If you want, I’ll join the technical kickoff Aug 11 to own the rollout sequence.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@pulsemed.com>

Cc: Kyle Dawson <kyle.d@pulsemed.com>
Date: Wed, Aug 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — this gives us what we need to start procurement. A couple items on our end:

- Procurement contact: Elena Park (elena.park@pulsemed.com) — she’ll expect a SOW + DocuSign link.
- Contract term: we’re aiming for a 12-month committed term to start; procurement may request net-30 billing.
- Staging: please provision the staging mirror and share creds/URL for our test account.

Once we have the final SOW + DocuSign I’ll route to Procurement and IT for SOC2 verification. Can you share the DocuSign link when ready?

Sara
